ukm:Metadata.dc:title: Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980
ukm:Metadata.dc:description: An Act to consolidate certain enactments relating to the jurisdiction of, and the practice and procedure before, magistrates’ courts and the functions of justices’ clerks, and to matters connected therewith, with amendments to give effect to recommendations of the Law Commission.

P1group.Title: Power to dispense with immediate payment.

P2para.Text:
A magistrates’ court by whose conviction or order a sum is adjudged to be paid may, instead of requiring immediate payment, allow time for payment, or order payment by
instalments.

Where a magistrates’ court has allowed time for payment, the court may, on application by or on behalf of the person liable to make the payment, allow further time or
order payment by instalments.

Where a court has ordered payment by instalments and default is made in the payment of any one instalment, proceedings may be taken as if the default had been made in the
payment of all the instalments then unpaid.
